title: The Boys in the Boat: Nine Americans and Their Epic Quest for Gold at the 1936 Berlin Olympics
author: Daniel James Brown
target_audience: Students of World War II and 20th-century history
General readers seeking human drama and perseverance
core_themes: Perseverance in the face of adversity
Teamwork and the power of community
The American Dream during the Great Depression
Sportsmanship and international politics on the eve of World War II
primary_purpose: To chronicle the journey of Joe Rantz and his University of Washington teammates as they rise from humble origins to international glory, highlighting their determination, collective spirit, and the larger historical forces at play in their quest for Olympic gold in Nazi Germany.

structure_format.narrative_style: Immersive, narrative nonfiction, blending personal biography, historical context, and sports action
structure_format.organization: Interwoven histories following the lives of Joe Rantz, his teammates, coach Al Ulbrickson, boatbuilder George Pocock, and events leading up to and including the 1936 Berlin Olympics
features: Rich historical detail and cultural context
Descriptions of rowing technique and team dynamics

key_concepts_lessons: Personal resilience and hope can overcome profound obstacles.
Teamwork requires trust, selflessness, and synchronized effort.
Socioeconomic disadvantage and hardship can fuel motivation and character.
Sports can serve as a platform for international unity and propaganda.
The pursuit of a dream can inspire individuals to transcend themselves for the good of the team.
Historical context deeply influences personal destinies.
notable_features: Vivid scenes of 1930s America and Berlin Olympics
Focus on both the technical and emotional aspects of rowing
Profiles of key figures (athletes, coaches, boatbuilders)
Exploration of Nazi Germany’s use of the Olympics for propaganda
cultural_historical_context: Set during the Great Depression and leading up to World War II, the book contrasts the economic hardships of the American Northwest with the pomp and propaganda of Nazi Germany. The 1936 Olympics were intended by Hitler to showcase Aryan supremacy, adding political stakes to the American team’s quest.
reception_impact: New York Times bestseller and critically acclaimed
Adopted in educational settings for lessons on history and character
Praised for its compelling storytelling and historical insight
Inspired adaptations, including a documentary and a feature film
Acknowledged for bringing lesser-known history to a wide audience
comparable_titles: Seabiscuit: An American Legend by Laura Hillenbrand
A Team of Rivals by Doris Kearns Goodwin
Flags of Our Fathers by James Bradley
